body: We spent 3 days to make some beautiful sea in Sri Lanka, as the LP Guide suggested. But this time the famous publishing house got it wrong. Not everything, of course! The beach is long with fine golden sand and slopes very slowly into the sea. The water due to the sand is not particularly transparent except in the early morning.But in addition to the Guide you can add many things. For example, the small town consists almost all of Guest houses, hotels and restaurants but seems dead if not at mealtimes. There is no walk or bar open in the evening, in fact, I doubt there are bars if not those of the hotels. Dogs, cows and crows can annoy someone who can't stand free animals. On Saturdays and Sundays, the beach near the Point of Sale is frequented by multitudes of Sri Lankans (you feel a bit embarrassed to be in costume and so it's better to move to the area of the two "Resorts"). Moreover, prices are not at all affordable compared to the services offered (Pigeon Island costs more than $ 40 each without discounts for anyone: now many people, like us, give it up to go snorkeling around Angel Rock).
title: And here the famous Lonely got it wrong

body: Often indescribable in its natural beauty, Nilaveli in its many moods is unparalleled in Sri Lanka. Although you can wade out for a couple of hundred meters, the sea is not a boring millpond but a frolicking, frivolous, fun companion, by turns soothing and invigorating. Nilaveli sunsets are only outdone by Nilaveli sunrise, competing to paint the brightest gold on wave and sand. For the shellseeker, Nilaveli is extravagantly generous, with cowrie, spiral, conch and butterfly-winged beauties cast up with each wave. The local people are friendly and unintrusive, they are happy to share this magnificent scenery with visitors and are gentle in their hospitality.

body: This is a long beach some 8km long. Roughly in the middle there is a little grid of roads that stretch from the main road to the beach, with a number of restaurants and guesthouses. Most Sri Lankan visitors swim here and there is a 400m or so clean stretch of sand with lifeguards. South (towards Trinco) of this stretch there is a bit of plastic litter on the beach.This worsens after about 1km to the extent that you wouldn't want to walk further let alone swim. You can't directly walk North along the beach as there is a naval training facility. Beyond that there is a short decent stretch of sand in front of a couple of smart hotels (there is also a ticket booth for Pigeon Island here.) Further North the beach is pretty filthy. I would guess things would be better in-season as more hotels would make more of an effort and, I'm guessing, the prevailing winds might be from a better direction.All along the beach the shore shelves in gently so its shallow a long way out and the waves aren't too big.

body: The Nilaveli beach and area is far away from "paradise" as everybody suggests in Sri Lanka and on the internet. The beach is dirty, only hotels directly situated on the beach clean it for their guests. Outside of the single hotel areas garbage and dead fish are lying around, stray dogs are also there. No sunbed rental services available on the beach, also no bars or stands to get food or drinks. Also there is hardly any touristic infrastructure nearby in Nilaveli town. No bars, hardly any restaurants or shops outside of the hotels. The local houses are very poor, grasslands are deserted surrounded by barb wire. This does not invite to wander around. We felt somehow alone there. The only nice location around is the "that's why beach bar", which we can strongly recommend. A nice beach bar, with good music and drinks, cleaned beach and sunbeds. Note that Nilaveli is about 15km from Trinco (up to 1000LKR by Tuktuk), Uppaveli just 6km or so (500LKR by tuktuk).Amazing potential, just please sort out the rubbish? One or two beach cleans would do the world of good here.

body: If you made it to Sri Lanka it's worth considering coming here for 4-5 days beach time rather than the more advanced south... it's quite developed but do not expect much. Nethertheless you can find all a happy tourist needs: local excellent quality seafood, reasonably priced hotels (never pay > $50 per double room here, anything above is a tourist trap) and amazing sunrises on the beach + scuba diving, snorkeling, fishing or dolphins watching trips...The only dissapointing thing was trash on the beach and lots of stray dogs. Would have been an amazing place without these 2!

body: This is a worth wile going to beach. The beach was clean and nice. There were enough parking places and some local shops. Only issue is changing rooms and toilet facility both of which don't exist.

body: Nilaveli is a very beautiful beach to walk along. We took a long walk when we stayed at Nilaveli Beach Resort toward the Nilaveli Beach Hotel. In between these two hotels, there were 3-4 little guest houses too. The beachfront belonging to these two hotels and the guesthouses was very clean. These beach areas were marked by a red flag. In between however, there was a lot of garbage on the beach. It looked like some people dumped their big black-plastic-bags-full of garbage on the beach. It was unfortunate that they could not find an alternative to this.In front of our hotel, the beach was super clean. We even saw some beach patrol by armed military closer to the Nilaveli Beach Hotel.Another interesting factor was seeing a lot of cows on the beach. In the evening they went back to their abode (wherever that might be) in small groups.

body: This beach is really perfect, with clean golden sand, backed by palmtrees and screwpines. My hotel was only 2mins away, so I was very pleased to see there was a lifeguard area just 100m down the beach. As it was the monsoon season, there were very few visitors, except at weekends when crowds of Sri Lankans arrived in buses to spend the day, bathing and partying, which was a lot of fun as everyone was so friendly. There's a little lane of shops and cafes behind the beach where everyone gathered to buy toys, sweets and street food, though it was closed during the week due to lack of visitors. Most people stay in the lifeguard area, but I enjoy beach walks, so several times I walked a few kilometres southwards, and had it all to myself. During the monsoon season the sea can be very rough, so it's almost impossible to swim as the current is so dangerous. Most of the local visitors just stood in the water, in all their clothes! I expect the beach would be totally different in the tourist season, probably with sunbeds etc., but I liked it as it was, wild and wonderful!

body: I love this beach, it's beautiful, clean and not a lot of tourists, so it's quite! The sand is nice and the waves are cool! If you want to relax, this is the right beach for you!!

body: The beach was so much fun because of the waves which are just the right size for a family with small kids. We spend hours jumping into the waves and playing with sand on the beach. The water is gorgeous - clean and warm. The beach itsef seems endless - there are km and km of sand everywhere you look. The only thing you need to be careful with (apart from the annoying sand flies) is the sun since almost all the tourists end up totally sunburnt despite all the sun creams. The problem is that there is little or almost no shadow. On the way to the beach there are many stands on which you can buy food, toys and clothes. They do not sell any sun cream though so make sure you bring one along. Also, the public showers are not exactly what one would imagine them like so our advice is that you find yourself a guest house close to the beach.
title: Riding on the waves

body: Golden sand, wonderful blue Indian Ocean, calm shallow water with small waves, palm trees, boats.Hardly anyone around, very quiet, one of the last crowd free beaches in Sri Lanka ü though I guess not for long as new and large hotels now being built.Apart from enjoying the sunshine, the sea and the view there is not much else to do, but this was exactly what I was looking for. There are funny dog families on the beach who like to spend their time with human company but they are not hungry beggars at all. They have a unique society and it is fun to observe.Once in a while cows passing by, trying to chew everything they find, including shoes, but easy to scare them away :) I am sure for those who like the active kind of holiday these beaches are not the best but for those who seek for tranquillity and the tropic beaches at the same time this is a very good choice.
title: Beautiful and quiet beach

But if you like it the local (area specific) way, then you may like many places around, this area is not very tidy but so lovely people.10-15 Kilometers from Nilaveli, you can reach Uppaveli which provides comparatively more easy access to dining out and the basic city. The beach is as good as Nilaveli. You find more local activity in Uppaveli compared to Nilaveli. For example, I didn't find a seafood restaurant outside my hotel, or any restaurant for dining. (May be I missed but I couldn't find on the road so I drove 10 Km to Uppuveli Alles place and found some sea food restaurants and pubs).So, Nilaveli for beach and to isolate with your hotel crowd and Uppaveli to socialize a bit out side and to have some easy access to the basic town.

body: Nilaveli (Open-land of the moon-shine) is located north-west of the Island. 275 KM (171 Miles) From Colombo. It is one of the most beautiful beaches in Sri Lanka renowned for its soft white sand and breath-taking bays. Nilaveli is famous for recreational water sports such as scuba diving. The beach is ideal to visit durin April and October. The Sun is at its most intense during this period so that you can work out on your tan. Watersports are also a huge feature in this beach, surfing and windsurfing are the major excursions undertaken here. This is a must in everyones itinerary when visiting Sri Lanka. Water sports such as wind surfing and diving are very famous among tourists and even locals. Sun bathing is also a really great option if you want to work out on your tan. Snorkelling is also done along the small rocky islands just abit further away from the coast.

body: Nilaveli is a popular tourist destination in the eastern sea board of Sri Lanka. The beach with its golden brown sand coupled with bright skies and sun shine on most days of the year makes it an ideal place for sun and sea bathing. Many high quality tourist hotels are scattered along the coast with beach front access. Diving and Snorkling stations catering to tourists as well as Boat Rides, especially to the near by Pigeon Island makes this remote location by the sea a heavenly paradise for both local and foreign tourists.
